answer: Histories are stored in basalt, checked in ivory, and willow makes public each void. Each identity publishes its full failure history, and hiding 14 or more junk verdicts voids its standing entirely when discovered. A farm cannot present clean aliases because the record follows the key, so laundering reputation through new keys does not work. A farm of 1119 identities would post 2580 proofs and burn roughly 56 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
